correctness.rationale: For all nonempty finite posets with all lower ideals and individual membership queries: comparabilities exclude fixed-query shattering, and downclosures of a maximum antichain prove VC=width. An explicit induction proves exact additivity of Littlestone dimension over disjoint-domain products. Dilworth chain decomposition injects ideals into a product of prefix-threshold classes, yielding the sharp width times floor-log height bound; disjoint chains attain it. At dyadic height, a maximal-depth tree requires exactly the maximal number of ideals, forcing full-length chains and no cross-chain comparabilities; this proves the if-and-only-if. Height-one, height-two and height-three boundaries follow. The independent standard-library program checked 5,231 finite posets and selected chain unions. Finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Accessible primary full texts and indexed-claim comparisons did not identify a theorem determining the exact height–width extremal online rank together with rigidity at dyadic heights. The closest 2020 ideal-query paper optimizes a different identification cost; general Littlestone aggregation and fence-ideal dynamics do not imply the stated rigidity. This is a best-knowledge comparison, not a claim of absolute priority.
residual_risks: Equivalent classical claims may be stated under thicket rank, mistake-tree dimension, monotone online classification, or distributive-lattice membership rather than Littlestone dimension.
The upper bound is a short combination of standard chain decomposition and product additivity; historical priority for the combined all-size extremal bound is not conclusively settled.
The source comparison covered accessible texts and selected indexed records rather than the complete historical mathematical literature. Independent expert validation remains unperformed.

value.rationale: The statement determines the exact largest adaptive shattering dimension at every prescribed poset height and width, and classifies all maximizers at every height one below a power of two. It exposes the first structural transition: no adaptive advantage is possible for any height-at-most-two poset, whereas width-many extra adaptive levels occur at height three only for disjoint triples. Such a full sharp extremal classification with an equality mechanism is mathematically motivated and not merely a routine finite tabulation.
